sections.heading: Major physical divisions — World, India & AP

blocks.text: India's relief comprises **four physiographic divisions — the Himalayas, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, and the Coastal Plains & Islands**. Within this, **Andhra Pradesh** occupies the south-east peninsula — the **Eastern Ghats, Coastal Plains and Rayalaseema plateau**.

rows: Young **fold mountains**; Himadri (Greater — Everest, Kanchenjunga), Himachal, Shiwalik; source of perennial rivers.
Ancient Gondwana; **Deccan trap, Western & Eastern Ghats, Central Highlands**; mineral-rich.
**Coastal Plains (Godavari-Krishna deltas), Eastern Ghats (Arma Konda highest), Rayalaseema plateau**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: physical divisions (India & AP)

items: **India — 6 physiographic divisions**: (1) **Himalayas** (young fold mts — Greater/Himadri with Everest & Kanchenjunga (India's highest = **Kanchenjunga**), Middle/Himachal, Outer/Shivaliks; longitudinal valleys **Duns**), (2) **Northern (Indo-Gangetic) Plains** (Bhabar-Terai-Bhangar-Khadar), (3) **Peninsular Plateau** (oldest — Deccan lava, Central Highlands, W. & E. Ghats), (4) **Indian Desert (Thar)**, (5) **Coastal Plains** (W. narrow Konkan-Malabar; E. broad deltaic), (6) **Islands** (Andaman & Nicobar — volcanic **Barren Island** = India's only active volcano; Lakshadweep — coral).

**Ghats**: **Western Ghats (Sahyadris)** higher/continuous (Anamudi = highest peak of peninsular India, Kerala; a **UNESCO/biodiversity hotspot**); **Eastern Ghats** lower/broken (highest **Arma Konda/Jindhagada, AP**).

**Andhra Pradesh geography**: ~**974 km coastline** (2nd longest after Gujarat); **Eastern Ghats** (Nallamala, Seshachalam, Papikonda); the **Krishna & Godavari deltas** ('rice bowl'); **Rayalaseema** semi-arid plateau; borders Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu & Bay of Bengal.
Four Indian divisions; AP = Eastern Ghats + Coastal Plains + Rayalaseema plateau.
Arma Konda (~1680 m) = highest peak in AP; Andaman = tectonic, Lakshadweep = coral.

prelimsPointers: India's four divisions — **Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Coastal Plains & Islands**.
Himalayan ranges (N→S) — **Himadri (Greater), Himachal (Lesser), Shiwalik (Outer)**.
**Peninsular Plateau** — oldest landmass (Gondwana); Deccan trap = black soil.
**Andaman & Nicobar** — of **tectonic/volcanic** origin (Barren Island — India's only active volcano); **Lakshadweep** — **coral**.
AP's three zones — **Coastal Plains, Eastern Ghats, Rayalaseema plateau**.
**Arma Konda (~1680 m)** — highest peak in AP (Eastern Ghats).
Western Ghats are continuous/higher; **Eastern Ghats are discontinuous** (cut by rivers).
India's 6 divisions: **Himalayas, N. Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Thar Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands**.
Highest peak in India = **Kanchenjunga (Sikkim)**; peninsular India's highest = **Anamudi (W. Ghats, Kerala)**.
**Barren Island (Andaman)** = India's only active volcano; **Lakshadweep** = coral islands.
AP coastline = **~974 km** (2nd longest); **Krishna-Godavari deltas** = 'rice bowl'; E. Ghats highest = **Arma Konda**.

glossary.definition: The ancient triangular plateau of southern India, part of the old Gondwana landmass.
The outermost, youngest Himalayan range bordering the northern plains.
The vast basaltic lava plateau of the peninsula, source of black cotton soil.

blocks.text: **Earthquakes** (sudden crustal shaking from tectonic movement) and **landslides** (downslope mass movement) are major **geophysical hazards**. India's seismic risk is mapped in **four zones**, with the Himalayas most vulnerable; landslides threaten hilly and Ghat regions.

rows: **Focus (hypocentre)** underground; **epicentre** above it; measured by **Richter (magnitude)** & **Mercalli (intensity)** scales; **seismograph**.
Mostly **plate tectonics (plate boundaries)**; also volcanic, reservoir-induced.
**Zones II–V**; **Zone V (highest risk)** — NE India, Himalayas, Kutch, A&N.
Common in **Himalayas, Western Ghats, NE**; triggered by rain, quakes, deforestation, slope-cutting.
AP is largely **Zone II-III** (relatively low seismicity); some Eastern-Ghat landslide risk.

items: **Cause**: India lies on the **Indian Plate colliding with the Eurasian Plate** → the Himalayas are seismically very active; measured by **Richter scale** (magnitude/energy) & **Mercalli** (intensity); focus/hypocentre & epicentre; the **seismograph** records waves.

**Seismic zoning (BIS)**: **Zone V** (very high — NE India, J&K, Himalayas, Kutch, A&N), **Zone IV** (high — Delhi, N. plains), **Zone III** (moderate — incl. much of AP), **Zone II** (low). ~**59% of India** is quake-prone.
**Major quakes**: Bhuj/Gujarat (2001), Latur (1993), Uttarkashi, Sikkim (2011), Bhagalpur.

**Landslides**: common in the **Himalayas & Western Ghats & NE** (steep slopes + heavy rain + deforestation + construction); **GSI** maps landslide hazard; AP's **Eastern Ghats/Araku** see local slides.
**Mitigation**: NDMA guidelines, earthquake-resistant building codes, hazard mapping, early-warning.
Focus vs epicentre; Richter (magnitude) vs Mercalli (intensity); Zone V = highest risk (Himalaya/NE/Kutch).
AP mostly low-seismic (Zone II-III).

prelimsPointers: **Focus/hypocentre** — origin underground; **epicentre** — point directly above on the surface.
**Richter scale** = magnitude (energy); **Mercalli scale** = intensity (damage); recorded by a **seismograph**.
Most earthquakes occur along **plate boundaries** (e.g. Himalayan collision zone).
India has **four seismic zones (II–V)**; **Zone V = highest risk** (NE India, Himalayas, Kutch, A&N).
**Landslides** — frequent in Himalayas, **Western Ghats**, NE; worsened by deforestation & road-cutting.
**Andhra Pradesh** lies mostly in **Zone II-III** (low-to-moderate seismicity).
**P, S and surface (L) waves** are generated; L-waves cause most damage.
Himalayan quakes = **Indian-Eurasian plate collision**; **Richter** (magnitude) vs **Mercalli** (intensity).
**Zone V** (highest risk): NE India, Kashmir, Kutch, A&N; ~**59% of India** quake-prone.
Major: **Bhuj (2001), Latur (1993), Sikkim (2011)**; **GSI** maps landslides.
Landslide-prone: **Himalayas, Western Ghats, NE**; mitigation via **NDMA**.

glossary.definition: The point on the Earth's surface directly above an earthquake's focus.
A logarithmic scale measuring the magnitude (energy) of an earthquake.
A region classified by earthquake risk; India uses Zones II (low) to V (highest).

sections.heading: Natural drainage, climatic regions & the monsoon

blocks.text: India's **drainage** divides into **Himalayan (perennial) and Peninsular (seasonal) rivers**; its **climate** is the **tropical monsoon** type, dominated by the **south-west and retreating (north-east) monsoons** that give the subcontinent its rhythm of seasons.

rows: **Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra** — perennial (snow+rain fed), antecedent, large deltas.
**Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi** (east-flowing, Bay of Bengal); **Narmada, Tapi** (west, rift, Arabian Sea).
**Differential heating, ITCZ shift, jet streams, El Nino**; SW monsoon (Jun-Sep) — Arabian Sea & Bay branches.
Godavari & Krishna are AP's great rivers; AP also gets **NE (retreating) monsoon** rain.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: drainage, climate & the monsoon

items: **Drainage**: **Himalayan (perennial, snow-fed)** — Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra (antecedent, gorges, deltas); **Peninsular (seasonal, rain-fed)** — east-flowing to Bay of Bengal (**Mahanadi, Godavari 'Dakshina Ganga', Krishna, Kaveri, Pennar**) with deltas; west-flowing to Arabian Sea (**Narmada, Tapi** in rift valleys — estuaries, no delta).

**Monsoon mechanism**: differential heating of land & sea; **ITCZ** shift; the **Tibetan Plateau** heating & **easterly jet stream**; **Somali/Findlater jet**; onset over **Kerala ~1 June**; SW monsoon (June–Sept) via **Arabian Sea & Bay of Bengal branches**; **NE (retreating) monsoon (Oct–Dec)** gives Tamil Nadu & coastal AP rain.
**El Nino/La Nina & IOD** modulate monsoon strength; 'break' & 'burst' of monsoon; Mawsynram/Cherrapunji = wettest (orographic).
**AP**: coastal AP gets both SW & NE monsoon; **Rayalaseema is rain-shadow/semi-arid**; cyclone-prone Bay of Bengal coast.
Himalayan (perennial) vs Peninsular (seasonal); Narmada/Tapi flow west (rift valleys).
SW monsoon = 75% of rain; AP depends on the NE (retreating) monsoon too.

prelimsPointers: **Himalayan rivers** — Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra (perennial, snow-fed).
**Peninsular rivers** — **Godavari (largest), Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi** (east-flowing); **Narmada & Tapi** flow **west** (rift valleys).
**SW monsoon (Jun-Sep)** brings ~**75%** of India's rain; two branches — **Arabian Sea & Bay of Bengal**.
**ITCZ (monsoon trough), jet streams, El Nino** modulate the monsoon.
**Mawsynram/Cherrapunji** (Meghalaya) — wettest places on Earth.
**Retreating (NE) monsoon (Oct-Dec)** gives rain to the **AP-Tamil Nadu coast**.
**Godavari & Krishna** are AP's main rivers (deltaic rice bowl).
Himalayan rivers **perennial**; peninsular **seasonal**; **Narmada & Tapi** flow **west** (rift valleys, estuaries).
**Godavari** = 'Dakshina Ganga', largest peninsular river; SW monsoon onsets **Kerala ~1 June**.
**NE (retreating) monsoon (Oct-Dec)** waters Tamil Nadu & coastal AP.
Monsoon drivers: **ITCZ shift, Tibetan Plateau heating, jet streams, ENSO/IOD**.

glossary.definition: The seasonal reversal of winds bringing India's rainfall, chiefly the SW monsoon (Jun-Sep).
A seasonal, rain-fed river of the plateau (e.g. Godavari, Krishna).
The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone whose seasonal shift drives the monsoon.

blocks.text: India's **natural vegetation** grades with rainfall from **tropical evergreen to thorn forests**, protected through a network of **national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves and tiger/elephant reserves** — with important sites in **Andhra Pradesh**.

rows: **Tropical evergreen (heavy rain), deciduous (monsoon — most widespread), thorn/scrub (arid), montane, mangrove (Sundarbans)**.
**National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves, Conservation/Community Reserves**.
Tiger reserves (Corbett — first); India holds ~70% of wild tigers.
**Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (largest), Papikonda & Sri Venkateswara NP, Coringa & Kolleru sanctuaries, Seshachalam Biosphere**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: vegetation, parks & sanctuaries

items: **Forest types (by rainfall)**: **Tropical evergreen** (>200 cm — W. Ghats, NE, A&N — rosewood, ebony), **Deciduous/monsoon** (most widespread — moist & dry; teak, sal), **Thorn/scrub** (<70 cm — Thar, Rayalaseema — acacia, khejri), **Montane** (Himalayas — oak, deodar, alpine), **Mangrove/littoral** (**Sundarbans** largest, Godavari-Krishna, Pichavaram).
**Protected-area categories**: Biosphere Reserves (18), National Parks (~100+), Wildlife Sanctuaries (~570+), **Tiger Reserves (Project Tiger 1973)**, Elephant Reserves, Ramsar wetlands.

**AP protected areas**: **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve** (India's largest tiger reserve), **Sri Venkateswara NP, Papikonda NP, Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) NP**; **Coringa** (mangroves), **Rollapadu** (Great Indian Bustard), **Pulicat** (lagoon/flamingos), **Kolleru** (Ramsar); **Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve** (red sanders).
**India State of Forest Report (FSI, biennial)**: forest+tree cover ~**24-25%** of area (target 33% per National Forest Policy 1988).
Vegetation by rainfall: evergreen→deciduous(most common)→thorn; mangrove = Sundarbans/Coringa.
AP: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (largest tiger reserve), Coringa mangrove, Kolleru birds.

prelimsPointers: **Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forest** — the most widespread type in India.
**Tropical evergreen** — Western Ghats, NE, A&N (heavy rain); **thorn/scrub** — arid NW & Rayalaseema.
**Mangroves** — Sundarbans (largest), **Coringa (AP)**.
**National Park > Wildlife Sanctuary** in protection level; **Biosphere Reserves** (18 in India).
**Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam** — India's **largest tiger reserve** (AP-Telangana).
AP protected areas — **Papikonda, Sri Venkateswara NP; Coringa, Kolleru, Nelapattu, Pulicat sanctuaries; Seshachalam Biosphere**.
**Corbett** — India's first national park; **Project Tiger (1973)**.
Forest by rainfall: **evergreen (>200cm) → deciduous → thorn (<70cm)**; **Sundarbans** = largest mangrove.
**Project Tiger (1973)**; India forest+tree cover ~**24-25%** (FSI report); target **33%**.
AP: **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam** = India's largest tiger reserve; **Coringa** mangroves; **Rollapadu** (GIB); **Seshachalam** (red sanders).
**Pulicat & Kolleru** lakes (AP) — key bird habitats/Ramsar.
mainsAngles: Classify India's natural vegetation and describe its protected-area network.

glossary.definition: Monsoon forest that sheds leaves in the dry season — India's most widespread vegetation type.
A large protected area conserving biodiversity with sustainable human use (e.g. Seshachalam).
A protected area under Project Tiger; Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam is India's largest.

blocks.text: India's **soils** (eight major types), **rocks** (igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic) and **minerals** underpin agriculture and industry. **Alluvial and black soils** are the most fertile/extensive, and the peninsula (including **AP**) is a rich mineral storehouse.

rows: Northern plains & river deltas (incl. AP coast); most fertile — **rice, wheat, sugarcane**.
**Igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic**; AP — **barytes (Mangampet, world's largest), limestone, granite, mica, coal (Singareni)**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: soils, rocks & minerals

rows: Rice, wheat, sugarcane; Khadar (new) vs Bhangar (old).
Cashew, tea, coffee; used as brick.

items: **Rocks**: **Igneous** (from magma — granite, basalt/Deccan Traps), **Sedimentary** (layered — sandstone, limestone, coal — fossils), **Metamorphic** (heat/pressure — marble, slate, gneiss).

**Minerals**: **coal** (Gondwana — Jharkhand/Odisha/Chhattisgarh; ~**Singareni, Telangana/AP**), **iron ore** (Odisha-Jharkhand-Chhattisgarh, Bellary-Hospet), **bauxite, mica** (India leads — Jharkhand/AP), **mineral oil** (Mumbai High, KG Basin, Assam); AP is rich in **barytes (Mangampet — world's largest), limestone, mica, granite, uranium (Tummalapalle)**.
Soil-crop pairs: alluvial-rice, black-cotton, red-groundnut, laterite-cashew.
AP minerals: Mangampet barytes (world's largest), Singareni coal, granite exports.

prelimsPointers: **Alluvial soil** — most extensive & fertile; **black (regur)** — best for **cotton**.
**Red soil** — much of the peninsula/AP (iron oxide); **laterite** — leached, high-rainfall areas.
Three rock types — **igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic**.
**Mangampet (AP)** — world's largest **barytes** deposit.
**Singareni coalfields (Godavari valley)** — peninsular India's main coal.
AP also has **limestone (cement), granite, mica, bauxite, uranium (Tummalapalle)**.
**Black soil** is derived from the **Deccan lava (trap)**.
**Black (regur)** soil → **cotton** (Deccan lava); **alluvial** = most fertile/widespread; **laterite** = leached (cashew).
Rock types: **igneous (granite/basalt), sedimentary (coal/limestone, fossils), metamorphic (marble/gneiss)**.
**Deccan Traps** = basaltic lava (parent of black soil); coal = **Gondwana** fields.
AP minerals: **barytes (Mangampet — world's largest), uranium (Tummalapalle), limestone, mica, granite**.
mainsAngles: Describe the major soil types of India and their agricultural significance.

glossary.definition: Black cotton soil formed on the Deccan trap, ideal for cotton.
A leached, iron-rich soil of high-rainfall regions, suited to cashew and plantations.
A barium mineral used in oil drilling; AP's Mangampet is the world's largest deposit.
